structured.approach: I followed DE-02 in the data-engineering-steps skill. I read feat.tasks to find this lane's tasks: TSK-01 and TSK-02, both in ap_pipeline. The permission table is restricted, so I read it through the tool view, which says no secrets are required or granted for ap_pipeline. The hook blocks shell commands in this step, so I checked the code with Grep and Read. I searched the checkout for environment-variable, credential, Databricks and network patterns and found none. I also read pipeline.py, ingest.py, transform.py, dq.py, schedule.json and ci.py. For background I read three approved items in full with context_get, so each citation has a receipt: task.repo_access (revision 177b1da), feat.design (revision 722a98f; NF-10 purity, SE-4 no secrets added) and feat.clarifications (revision 36d4dac; CL-X9 synthetic data, no secrets). I rewrote task.secrets_scope in full, with names only. It records that no secret is required or granted and that no access request is needed. One question stays open and is non-blocking: whether the DE-13 scheduler will need a credential.

claims.text: The Data Engineering lane tasks are TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02), both in ap_pipeline.
The permission table states that no secrets are required or granted for the ap_pipeline repository.
TSK-02's delays_by_vendor is a pure function with no I/O. TSK-01 changes only transform.py, __init__.py and tests/test_pipeline.py. Neither task touches ingest.py, pipeline.py or schedule.json.
The pipeline takes the feed as text: run(csv_text) calls parse_feed, then to_model, then quality_report. It opens no connection to a source system.
A search of the ap_pipeline checkout for environment-variable, secret, credential, Databricks and network patterns found no match, and ci.py reads no environment variable or credential.
The design states that every new function is pure and in-memory, with no I/O and no network (NF-10). It adds no secrets or personal data (SE-4).
Test data is synthetic only, with no secrets or personal data (CL-X9).
Databricks or another workspace is not used by this lane, so no workspace credential is needed.
schedule.json sets frequency daily at 02:00 in Asia/Kolkata and is unchanged by this feature; no input names the scheduler platform or its credential needs.

open_questions: SSQ-1 (non-blocking): DE-13 will schedule the pipeline (schedule.json: daily, 02:00, Asia/Kolkata), but no input names the scheduler platform or says whether it needs a credential. Interim answer: no secret now; re-run DE-02 if DE-13 names a scheduler that needs one. Owner: Data engineering lead.
structured.summary: I rewrote task.secrets_scope for FEAT-ZD-48600. The lane's tasks, TSK-01 and TSK-02 in ap_pipeline, need no secrets, and the permission table grants none for the repository. The granted secret names are therefore "none", and no access request was raised. Four things back this up: the code reads no environment variables, credentials or network sources; the design keeps every new function pure and adds no secrets (NF-10, SE-4); test data is synthetic only (CL-X9); and the lane uses no Databricks. Both design files are now read in full with receipts. There are no blocking questions. One non-blocking question asks whether the DE-13 scheduler will need a credential.
